title: Mehtab Singh ((Praise Be to Mehtab Singh)

blocks.text: Dohra:
(Dear devout readers) listen to another episode, About Mehtab Singh (a great Singh Martyr), Whom Harbhagat2 (Niranjania) hailing from Jandiala, Had proceeded to take into Mughal's custody. (1)
lines: (Dear devout readers) listen to another episode,
About Mehtab Singh (a great Singh Martyr),
Whom Harbhagat2 (Niranjania) hailing from Jandiala,
Had proceeded to take into Mughal's custody.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Having been allotted a large contingent of Mughal troops, He proceeded to take Mehtab Singh into custody. Mehtab Singh being, always with a large contingent of Singhs, A smaller Mughal contingent could never arrest him. (2)
lines: Having been allotted a large contingent of Mughal troops,
He proceeded to take Mehtab Singh into custody.
Mehtab Singh being, always with a large contingent of Singhs,
A smaller Mughal contingent could never arrest him.

blocks.text: Mehtab Singh being a mighty warrior and a Singh perfect, His very name sent shivers down the enemy's spine. The Singhs, who put on their armour by swearing on Mehtab Singh's name, They would always remain prepared to do or die. (3)
lines: Mehtab Singh being a mighty warrior and a Singh perfect,
His very name sent shivers down the enemy's spine.
The Singhs, who put on their armour by swearing on Mehtab Singh's name,
They would always remain prepared to do or die.

blocks.text: The possible hideouts of Mehtab Singh the Mughal spies indicated, Were those raided by the troops of Harbhagat Niranjania. The Singhs having camouflaged themselves in the wilds, Mughal troops did feel scared of getting into the wild growth. (4)
lines: The possible hideouts of Mehtab Singh the Mughal spies indicated,
Were those raided by the troops of Harbhagat Niranjania.
The Singhs having camouflaged themselves in the wilds,
Mughal troops did feel scared of getting into the wild growth.

blocks.text: They would kill an odd Singh whom they came across, Who would always fight to the finish, killing so many Mughals. As Harbhagat kept on looking for Mehtab Singh for many days, Mehtab Singh came to hear about this witch hunt from Singhs. (5)
lines: They would kill an odd Singh whom they came across,
Who would always fight to the finish, killing so many Mughals.
As Harbhagat kept on looking for Mehtab Singh for many days,
Mehtab Singh came to hear about this witch hunt from Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Mehtab Singh heard of Bhai Taru Singh's being taken a prisoner, The Mughal officials having taken him to the city of Lahore. With Bhai Taru Singh making a supreme sacrifice of his life, A turmoil was bound to erupt at the Divine Court. (6)
lines: Mehtab Singh heard of Bhai Taru Singh's being taken a prisoner,
The Mughal officials having taken him to the city of Lahore.
With Bhai Taru Singh making a supreme sacrifice of his life,
A turmoil was bound to erupt at the Divine Court.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Laying the blame for his sacrifice squarely on Lahore's Nawab, Bhai Taru Singh would make the Nawab face Divine retribution. Keeping his faith with hair intact till the last breath, Bhai Taru Singh would lay the blame squarely on the Mughals. (7)
lines: Laying the blame for his sacrifice squarely on Lahore's Nawab,
Bhai Taru Singh would make the Nawab face Divine retribution.
Keeping his faith with hair intact till the last breath,
Bhai Taru Singh would lay the blame squarely on the Mughals.

blocks.text: Acquiescing and abiding with the will Divine, Would Taru Singh succeed in proving the Mughals guilty. Praise be to the Singh who wages a religious war, Praise be to him who sacrifices accusing the Mughals. (8)
lines: Acquiescing and abiding with the will Divine,
Would Taru Singh succeed in proving the Mughals guilty.
Praise be to the Singh who wages a religious war,
Praise be to him who sacrifices accusing the Mughals.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Most successful and glorious is the act of dying, Among all the ways of shedding one's mortal frame. Provided he keeps his faith and his religious vows, Though he may perish while fighting the Mughals. (9)
lines: Most successful and glorious is the act of dying,
Among all the ways of shedding one's mortal frame.
Provided he keeps his faith and his religious vows,
Though he may perish while fighting the Mughals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Praise, more praise be to Bhai Mani Singh3 , Who got his body dismembered to keep his faith. Praise be to Bhai Dyal Singh of Shahesar, Who got himself crushed among spoked wheels for his faith. (10)
lines: Praise, more praise be to Bhai Mani Singh3 ,
Who got his body dismembered to keep his faith.
Praise be to Bhai Dyal Singh of Shahesar,
Who got himself crushed among spoked wheels for his faith.

blocks.text: Praise be to Subeg Singh Jambar4 and his son, Who kept meditating even while being crushed on a rack. Praise be to all those Singhs who kept their faith, Who shed their mortal frame in the name of their Guru. (11)
lines: Praise be to Subeg Singh Jambar4 and his son,
Who kept meditating even while being crushed on a rack.
Praise be to all those Singhs who kept their faith,
Who shed their mortal frame in the name of their Guru.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hardly any noble deed was he (Mehtab Singh) doing, Spending whole of his life remaining incognito. How could he hope to sit in the line of great martyrs, In the Divine court of the Almighty after leaving this world? (12)
lines: Hardly any noble deed was he (Mehtab Singh) doing,
Spending whole of his life remaining incognito.
How could he hope to sit in the line of great martyrs,
In the Divine court of the Almighty after leaving this world?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

How could he join the ranks of those great Singh martyrs, How could he join the company of the blessed ones? Human body being mortal and never enduring forever, He had wasted most of his life in mundane affairs. (13)
lines: How could he join the ranks of those great Singh martyrs,
How could he join the company of the blessed ones?
Human body being mortal and never enduring forever,
He had wasted most of his life in mundane affairs.

blocks.text: Why should he shed his mortal frame without fighting the Mughals, Why should he miss the opportunity of attaining a Martyr's status? Damned be a person taking human birth and then dying, Without shedding his mortal frame while fighting against Mughals. (14)
lines: Why should he shed his mortal frame without fighting the Mughals,
Why should he miss the opportunity of attaining a Martyr's status?
Damned be a person taking human birth and then dying,
Without shedding his mortal frame while fighting against Mughals.

blocks.text: Thus, contemplating his death on these (patriotic) lines, Mehtab Singh readied himself to join Bhai Taru Singh. Bhai Taru Singh being one of his intimate friends, He must join his company after shedding his mortal frame. (15)
lines: Thus, contemplating his death on these (patriotic) lines,
Mehtab Singh readied himself to join Bhai Taru Singh.
Bhai Taru Singh being one of his intimate friends,
He must join his company after shedding his mortal frame.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Addressing the fellow Singhs of his own contingent, He asked them to join some other contingent of the Singhs. He himself would proceed in the direction of Lahore, So that he could join his colleague Bhai Taru Singh. (16)
lines: Addressing the fellow Singhs of his own contingent,
He asked them to join some other contingent of the Singhs.
He himself would proceed in the direction of Lahore,
So that he could join his colleague Bhai Taru Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

With these words, Mehtab Singh proceeded towards Lahore, Carrying a single wooden staff after disarming himself. Arms being meant for fighting on the field of battle, He would present himself before the Nawab only with a stick. (17)
lines: With these words,
Mehtab Singh proceeded towards Lahore,
Carrying a single wooden staff after disarming himself.
Arms being meant for fighting on the field of battle,
He would present himself before the Nawab only with a stick.

blocks.text: The spot where Harbhagat Niranjania was hunting for him, Mehtab Singh arrived at that spot on his own. They arrested him instantly at the first sight, And loaded him on a cart after putting his body in fetters. (18)
lines: The spot where Harbhagat Niranjania was hunting for him,
Mehtab Singh arrived at that spot on his own.
They arrested him instantly at the first sight,
And loaded him on a cart after putting his body in fetters.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After handcuffing both of Mehtab Singh's hands, They placed his handcuffed hands on a flat board. Fixing an iron peg in the wooden board of the cart, They chained his handcuffed hands to the fixed iron peg. (19)
lines: After handcuffing both of Mehtab Singh's hands,
They placed his handcuffed hands on a flat board.
Fixing an iron peg in the wooden board of the cart,
They chained his handcuffed hands to the fixed iron peg.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, pressing his arms between two wooden poles, They numbed his muscles by stopping the blood circulation. Carrying him on a cart to his native village, They assembled the whole village populace to identify him. (20)
lines: Thereafter, pressing his arms between two wooden poles,
They numbed his muscles by stopping the blood circulation.
Carrying him on a cart to his native village,
They assembled the whole village populace to identify him.

blocks.text: Mehtab Singh, with a sly gesture of his little finger, Prohibited the villagers from identifying his identity. In case, any villager identified Mehtab Singh, Harbhagat would get the whole village populace converted to Islam. (21)
lines: Mehtab Singh, with a sly gesture of his little finger,
Prohibited the villagers from identifying his identity.
In case, any villager identified Mehtab Singh,
Harbhagat would get the whole village populace converted to Islam.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Arriving at Lahore with Mehtab Singh in his custody, Harbhagat Niranjania informed the Nawab of Lahore. He pleaded for Mehtab Singh's execution on the spoked wheels, After the latter had had a glimpse of Bhai Taru Singh's face. (22)
lines: Arriving at Lahore with Mehtab Singh in his custody,
Harbhagat Niranjania informed the Nawab of Lahore.
He pleaded for Mehtab Singh's execution on the spoked wheels,
After the latter had had a glimpse of Bhai Taru Singh's face.

blocks.text: The way Mehtab Singh had resolved to make a supreme sacrifice, He placed himself between the two spoked wheels voluntarily. Praise be to the blessed Singh and his noble sacrifice, Who made the supreme sacrifice to keep his Sikh faith. (23)
lines: The way Mehtab Singh had resolved to make a supreme sacrifice,
He placed himself between the two spoked wheels voluntarily.
Praise be to the blessed Singh and his noble sacrifice,
Who made the supreme sacrifice to keep his Sikh faith.

blocks.text: Bhai Taru Singh felt ecstatic after hearing of this act, That Mehtab Singh had voluntarily made a supreme sacrifice. Priase, Praise unbounded be to great Mehtab Singh, Who had joined him (Bhai Taru Singh) in the noble cause voluntarily. (24)
lines: Bhai Taru Singh felt ecstatic after hearing of this act,
That Mehtab Singh had voluntarily made a supreme sacrifice.
Priase,
Praise unbounded be to great Mehtab Singh,
Who had joined him (Bhai Taru Singh) in the noble cause voluntarily.
